meru-8-13-supply-package-vs-first-half-s:
The Korean government put out two property packages together on August 13.
One is a fast-track housing supply plan meant to steady the rental and resale markets, the other a comprehensive finance package aimed at the property market.

What sits at the very top of the announcement is not a new target but an old one.
It is a line promising to improve delivery on the 1.35 million housing starts in the Seoul metropolitan area set out in the September 7, 2025 package.

@@BAR@@2026 starts target, Seoul metro area|269,000 homes|26.9|Actual starts, first half of 2026|65,204 homes|6.52@@That is the tally at the halfway mark. To reach the target, more than 200,000 homes must break ground in the remaining six months. Of the 65,204, only 13,121 were in Seoul itself.@@Original August 13 announcement as compiled by Meru, accessed 2026-08-14

The reason an existing target was restated at the top lies in that number.
Large sites such as the Yongsan International Business District, the Taereung golf course and the Gwacheon racecourse land are stalled against opposition from local governments and residents.

## When do the 230,000 arrive

The second item placed near the top is an additional 230,000 homes for the metropolitan area.
The word additional is explicit, so it is counted separately from the earlier target.

@@SHARE@@Sites already named|27,000 homes|2.7|To be announced within 2026|73,000 homes|7.3|Breaking ground after 2030|110,000 homes|11|Timing undecided|20,000 homes|2@@Almost half of the newly added volume sits beyond 2030. Measured against the 2030 horizon, the earlier 1.35 million becomes something closer to 1.47 million.@@Original August 13 announcement as compiled by Meru, accessed 2026-08-14

@@REF@@S. Korea vows to start building 230,000 houses in 5 years amid housing affordability crisis (The Korea Herald, 2026-08-13)|https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10840159|https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/news/cms/2026/08/13/rcv.YNA.20260812.PYH2026081214410001300_T1.jpg

That report lists the breakdown of the 27,000 homes whose locations are fixed.
There are 1,000 in Yeomchang-dong in western Seoul, 21,700 around Wabu-eup in Namyangju, and 4,500 around Jangji-dong in Gwangju city, both in Gyeonggi province.

Most of the newly added volume sits outside Seoul.

## The lending side moved first

The clause that bites immediately is not one that tightens but one that loosens.
The ceiling on how much banks may grow household lending in a year was raised from 1.5% to 3.0%.
Relocation loans taken when a home is vacated for redevelopment, interim payment loans that spread the purchase price, and closing loans paid at move-in were pulled out of that ceiling altogether.

@@REF@@Korea Doubles Household Loan Growth Target to 3%, Easing Mortgage Squeeze (Seoul Economic Daily English, 2026-08-13)|https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/08/13/korea-doubles-2025-household-loan-growth-target-to-3|https://wimg.sedaily.com/news/cms/2026/08/13/news-p.v1.20260806.cf902aeb0974402e9d7df7646d865e63_P1.jpg

That report puts the effect of doubling the ceiling at roughly 30 trillion won of extra lending capacity in the second half.
The purpose of the clause is to stop bank branches from running out of mortgage quota.

On the tightening side sits the jeonse deposit loan.
Jeonse is the Korean lease in which a tenant hands the landlord a large lump sum instead of paying monthly rent, and the loan funds that sum.
A single-home owner who holds a flat in a regulated metropolitan district, does not live in it and rents it out loses access to new guarantees, and existing loans will not be rolled over at maturity.
The line between speculation and not is drawn on residence history.
It counts as speculation only if neither the owner nor the spouse has ever lived in the flat.

Read the other way, one day of registered residence by either spouse takes the household out of the rule.
The Seoul Economic Daily report notes the same carve-out, that a residency history for either spouse does not meet the speculation standard.
Because a landlord can clear the bar by moving in briefly between tenants, Meru expects the measure to do little.

## What the August 13 package leaves behind

Supply slid past 2030 while the borrowing ceiling was lifted now.
So does that combination press prices down or hold them up.

For younger buyers a door opened.
Someone aged 39 or under earning no more than 70 million won a year can borrow up to 80% of the price on a first home.
Flats in apartment complexes are excluded, so this applies only to non-apartment housing such as low-rise villas priced at 400 million won or less.

The answer turns on the starts tally early next year.
Reach the annual target and last September's package held its first year, fall short and what remains is six months in which the money available to borrow grew while the housing did not.
jukan-nanya-ccl-20-25pct-glass-cloth-sin:
A price notice that Nan Ya Plastics' electronic materials division sent to customers in August has been made public.
CCL and prepreg prices go up 20 to 25%, applied to shipments from September 1.

The notice says that amid a broad rise in raw material costs the shortage of glass cloth in particular has been severe, that the supply gap widened month by month, and that procurement costs ran beyond control.
Copper is not what it leads with.

## Why glass and not copper

CCL is the board that sits underneath a printed circuit board.
Glass fibre woven into cloth is impregnated with resin and cured, then faced with copper foil, and that is CCL. The half-finished state before curing is prepreg.
Put simply, the glass cloth is the skeleton of the board and the copper is the wiring drawn on top of it.
Without the skeleton there is nowhere to draw the wiring.

@@BAR@@Korea CCL import price, March 2026|$20,728 per tonne|20728|Same month a year earlier|$11,880 per tonne|11880@@The weight the base material carries in the cost of a board grew by this multiple in a single year. Korea has kept these statistics since 2000 and this is the first time the figure has entered this range.@@TrendForce, 2026-05-06, citing Korean trade statistics · retrieved 2026-08-14

@@REF@@CCL Market Tightens as Korea Import Prices Reportedly Rise 74.5% YoY (TrendForce, 2026-05-06)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/05/06/news-ai-demand-tightens-ccl-supply-drives-advance-orders-price-hikes-and-expansion/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/03182221/Chip-FREEPIK-20260203-624x351.jpg

That report says a Seoul board maker placed advance orders with two Taiwanese suppliers worth more than five times its typical monthly usage.
That is not the behaviour of a buyer negotiating a price. It is the behaviour of one reserving a place in line.

## One company does the weaving

Boards for AI servers move to glass cloth with a lower dielectric constant as signals get faster.
Japan's Nittobo holds roughly 90% of that T-glass segment, and 60 to 70% of the NER-glass grade below it.

@@REF@@Glass Fiber Cloth: The Underlying Material Shortage in AI Infrastructure (TrendForce Insights, 2026-04-30)|https://insights.trendforce.com/p/glass-fiber-cloth-shortage|https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!5wj0!,w_1200,h_675,c_fill,f_jpg,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep,g_auto/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Faa7059d6-c21f-4cce-9e7f-9b322dfbe66f_1672x941.png

The same analysis expects that company's new capacity to start running by the middle of 2027 at the earliest.
Meanwhile consumption keeps climbing, as Nvidia's Rubin generation raises both substrate area and layer count and cableless designs add midplane and backplane demand.

Reuters reported in November 2025 that the two companies had joined forces to expand special glass cloth production.
The side sending the increase notice is also the side that has decided to make the material itself.

When supply is fixed for more than a year while demand grows, raising the price does not produce more material.
Being unable to buy because it is expensive and being unable to buy because there is none left are different problems, and money does not solve the second one.

## What September 1 decides

@@TIME@@2025-11|Nan Ya notifies customers of an 8% rise in CCL and prepreg prices|2026-03|A Seoul board maker front-loads orders worth over five times its monthly usage with Taiwanese suppliers|2026-04-28|Kingboard lifts FR-4 grades by 10%, its fourth increase of the year|2026-08|Nan Ya sends another increase notice|>2026-09-01|Applied from this shipping date@@The gaps between increases got shorter and the steps got larger. That shape is what separates passing on a cost from rationing a material.@@DigiTimes and TrendForce reporting · retrieved 2026-08-14

If board makers pass the increase straight through to set makers, it ends as a cost transfer.
If they cannot, margins take it, and from that point orders go to whoever secured glass cloth.
What decides this is not the size of the increase but when Nittobo's new line runs.
If it starts in the middle of 2027 this increase stays a one-year cost wave. If that date slips again, the schedule of every product that uses a circuit board is tied to a single kind of woven glass.
elerian-30y-auction-highest-since-2001-a:
The US Treasury sold $25 billion of 30-year bonds on August 13, and the high yield was 5.2%.
That is the highest since 5.5% in August 2001.

@@REF@@U.S. set to pay most for 30-year debt in quarter of a century (Fortune, 2026-08-13)|https://fortune.com/2026/08/13/us-debt-treasury-30-year-highest-25-years/|https://fortune.com/img-assets/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/GettyImages-2287747676-1-e1786633388665.jpg?resize=1200,600

The auction itself cleared without difficulty.
A portfolio manager quoted in that piece noted that a successful auction should not be confused with strong structural demand for long-duration assets.

## Why the bond disappeared last time

The circumstances behind the previous record, in 2001, were the reverse of today's.
The budget was in surplus, the government did not need to borrow that much, and in the autumn of that year the Treasury announced it would stop issuing the 30-year bond altogether.

@@REF@@30-year Treasury bonds to return Feb. 9 (NBC News, 2006)|https://www.nbcnews.com/news/amp/wbna11133022|https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/v1696280772/newsgroup-logos/nbcnews/social/primary-white-1680x840.png

Selling resumed on February 9, 2006, and that first auction back was $14 billion.
What goes out in a single sale today is far larger.

@@TIME@@2001-08|A 30-year auction sets the previous high in yield|2001-10|The Treasury announces it will stop issuing the bond, citing budget surpluses|2006-02-09|Issuance resumes after more than four years|2026-08-13|The bond sells at the highest yield since that record|>2026-11|The next quarterly refunding announcement@@The same level of yield has now been passed twice. The first time there was money to spare and the bond was retired. The second time there is not enough, and that is the price being paid.@@US Treasury announcements · NBC News reporting · retrieved 2026-08-14

## The bill at $3 billion a day

Why the long end holds where it does becomes easier to see from the interest bill.

@@CHK@@Interest on the debt, fiscal year to date|$1.17 trillion|Change from a year earlier|+15%|Treasury debt outstanding|$31 trillion@@Maturing paper keeps rolling over at higher rates. The author's premise, that demand for long money is heavy, is carried by these numbers.@@Fortune, 2026-08-13, citing Treasury data · retrieved 2026-08-14

Put simply, the balance on the card has not merely grown. The rate on it went up while the balance kept revolving.
The Treasury has leaned issuance toward shorter maturities to defer that burden, which brings each rollover around more often.

## What El-Erian posted that same morning

Hours before he relayed the auction result, El-Erian wrote that there is a second queue.
Citing the FT's Alphaville column, he reported that the hyperscalers' purchase commitments have reached $1.5 trillion, and said these sit on top of large government financing needs.
A purchase commitment is money already contracted to buy chips, compute, and the power and equipment that run a data centre.

Not all of that reaches the bond market.
But a commitment has to turn into cash eventually, and one route to that cash is corporate issuance.
When a government and the technology companies look for long money at the same window, the borrower is not the side that sets the price.

The thing that decides this is the November refunding.
If the Treasury lifts the share of long-dated issuance, today's yield is confirmed as a price made by supply, and if it keeps leaning on bills, the price of long money will swing more on the issuance calendar of corporations.

meru-maxell-337-institution-vs-netlist-m:
On August 12 the US International Trade Commission opened a new investigation into Samsung Electronics and Samsung Electronics America.
It was instituted on a complaint from Japan's Maxell and carries the docket number 337-TA-1516.

@@REF@@USITC Institutes Section 337 Investigation of Certain Mobile Electronic Devices (US International Trade Commission, 2026-08-12)|https://www.usitc.gov/press_room/news_release/2026/er0812_69071.htm

The commission's notice records July 24 as the date Maxell filed its amended complaint, and the relief sought is a limited exclusion order together with cease and desist orders.

The same day, a second complaint arrived at the same commission.
This one came from Netlist, and it names Micron, Supermicro, HPE and Lenovo.
Netlist is the company that closed a settlement with Samsung on August 5.

## Why the border and not a fine

Section 337 sits in the Tariff Act of 1930.
Its purpose is to keep infringing goods from entering the country and harming domestic industry, so this commission does not award damages.

@@FLOW@@Complaint|Maxell filed on six patents in December 2024 and lodged an amended complaint on July 24, 2026|Institution|The commission opened docket 337-TA-1516 on August 12, and a target completion date is set within 45 days|Final determination|Unlike a court case that runs through three levels of appeal, this usually concludes in 16 to 18 months|Exclusion order|Customs stops the goods at the border, and inventory already inside the country is frozen by a cease and desist order@@A court collects money from the losing side. At the end of this path there is nothing left to sell. That is why companies that make their living from patents reach for this commission before they reach for a court.

Put simply, a court makes you pay after the crash. The commission keeps the car from crossing the border at all.

## The month the customers became respondents

Netlist is a memory module company in Irvine, California.
It holds patents that sit on server memory and HBM standards, and it has earned more from defending those patents than from selling product.

@@TIME@@2015-11|Signs a joint development and licensing agreement with Samsung|2023|An East Texas jury awards $303 million for infringement of five patents, with $118 million added in 2024|2026-07|Google, Nvidia, Broadcom and Supermicro are pulled in as co-respondents at the commission|2026-08-05|Samsung settles with a five-year licence worth up to $897 million|>2026-09-26|Deadline for the target completion date in the Maxell case to be set, 45 days after institution@@A settlement Samsung had resisted for three years after the verdict arrived one month after its customers appeared on the respondent list.

On the verdict alone Samsung had no reason to hurry.
While the appeal bought time, the commission case moved forward, and on that docket sat the companies that sell products with Samsung HBM inside them.
Once Google's TPUs and Supermicro's GPU servers can be stopped at customs, the counterparty in the negotiation is no longer Samsung alone.

## The seat Micron now occupies

The complaint Netlist filed on August 12 walks that same sequence from the first step.
The accused products are DDR5 RDIMMs and MRDIMMs, and four patents are asserted.
The respondents are not only Micron but Supermicro, HPE and Lenovo, the companies that buy those modules and slot them into servers.

@@REF@@Netlist Files Patent Infringement Action Against Micron in the U.S. International Trade Commission (PR Newswire, 2026-08-12)|https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/netlist-files-patent-infringement-action-against-micron-in-the-us-international-trade-commission-302849003.html|https://mmx.prnewswire.com/media/MS1868604/Netlist-Inc-logo.jpg?id=OA2859274&p=facebook

Netlist's release says its major competitors have licensed the patents for years while Micron continues to use them without authorisation.
With Samsung and SK hynix each having settled their way out, that sentence points at the one company left.

What remains on the Samsung side is the Maxell case.
It is confined to phones and tablets, and feature patents covering cameras or unlocking are easier to design around than a memory standard.
Whether that investigation ever reaches the customs desk, or simply sets the price of a settlement, is a different question from the one Netlist is asking.
What separates the two cases is not the number of patents but the list of respondents.
Maxell has two names on it, both of them Samsung. Netlist put the buyers on its list from the first day.
With no customers on the list, delay favours the defendant. With customers on it, delay turns into cost.
serenity-aehr-22m-wafer-level-burn-in-fo:
Aehr Test Systems said on 12 August that it had received a $22 million follow-on order for wafer-level burn-in systems used on AI processors.
The systems ship to a manufacturing partner in Taiwan over the next six months.

@@REF@@Aehr Receives $22 Million Follow-On Order for AI Processor Wafer-Level Burn-In Systems (Aehr Test Systems press release, 2026-08-12)|https://www.aehr.com/2026/08/aehr-receives-22-million-follow-on-order-for-ai-processor-wafer-level-burn-in-systems/|https://www.aehr.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/press-releases-img.png

Burn-in means deliberately holding a freshly made chip at high voltage and heat.
Electronics that fail tend to fail early in life, so the point is to kill the weak parts inside the factory rather than in the field.

Add "wafer level" and it means that stress is applied to the whole 300mm disc, before the chips are cut apart.

## Why this test grew with AI chips

An AI accelerator bonds several HBM stacks onto a compute die to make one assembly.
An HBM stack is 12 to 16 thin memory dies piled up, and memory accounts for close to half the cost of the finished part.

@@REF@@HBM Shifts Testing Left To Preserve AI Chip Yield (Semiconductor Engineering, 2026-05-12)|https://semiengineering.com/hbm-shifts-testing-left-to-preserve-ai-chip-yield/|https://semiengineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Ann-5_11-Fig-3.jpg

In that piece a Synopsys engineer says HBM failures are the number one cause of GPU failures in data centres.
When one memory die inside an expensive assembly goes, the whole assembly goes with it.
That is why the test keeps moving earlier rather than later.

## An order worth half of last year

@@CHK@@Fiscal 2026 revenue|$50.0 million|Backlog at end of May|$80.6 million|Fiscal 2027 company guidance|$130-150 million@@This one order equals 44% of last fiscal year's revenue. Because the systems ship across six months, the revenue lands across several quarters.@@Aehr Test Systems fiscal 2026 results (2026-07-14) and the 12 August press release, retrieved 2026-08-13

This company's revenue used to come from testing silicon carbide chips for electric vehicles, and when that demand cooled fiscal 2026 revenue actually fell 15%.

The original post introduces it as a small company worth about $1.1 billion, but that figure comes from an earlier post quoted inside it.

Interest charged on US government debt over the past twelve months came to $1.37 trillion, a record.
But lining that number up against Social Security spending to see which is bigger does not work. The two are not measured with the same ruler.

@@REF@@US July deficit tops $432 billion as outlays grow (Reuters, 2026-08-12)|https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/us-july-deficit-tops-432-180448445.html|https://storage.googleapis.com/media.mwcradio.com/mimesis/2026-08/12/2026-08-12T180448Z_2_LYNXMPEM7B1FE_RTROPTP_3_USA-TRUMP-LABOR-SENATE.JPG

Reuters reports from the July Monthly Treasury Statement that the month's deficit was $432 billion, a July record, and that the fiscal 2026 shortfall over ten months is $1.799 trillion. Interest is the fastest-growing item inside that gap.

## Interest goes by two names

The "interest expense on the public debt" that Treasury publishes each month adds up the interest on every Treasury security outstanding.
That includes the interest on securities held by the Social Security and Medicare trust funds.

That portion is money the government moves from one pocket to another and writes down as interest.
No cash leaves the government, so the budget does not count it as interest at all.

What the budget carries instead is a different number, net interest, with that portion taken out.
Fiscal 2024 shows the gap plainly. Gross interest was $1.133 trillion and net interest was $880 billion.
In a single year, two figures both called interest sat $253 billion apart.

@@BAR@@Social Security outlays|$1.569T|1569|Gross interest|$1.229T|1229|Net interest in the budget|$1.028T|1028@@The figure Bilello cites is the trailing-twelve-month version of the middle bar. The one that competes with Social Security for size is the bottom bar.@@Fiscal 2025 actuals, CBO Monthly Budget Review (November 2025) and US Treasury Fiscal Data (accessed 2026-08-13)

## Net interest is already number two

Correcting the number does not shrink the story.
In fiscal 2025 Social Security was the largest line at $1.569 trillion, and net interest came next at $1.028 trillion.
Medicare at $992 billion and national defense at $868 billion sat below it.
Interest has already passed health care and defense to become the second-largest item in the budget.

The cause is not only a bigger pile of debt. The price of carrying it went up.
The average rate on marketable Treasury debt rose from 1.5% in July 2021 to 3.4% in July 2026, more than doubling.
Put simply, rolling the same stack of debt costs twice what it cost five years ago, and the stack grew as well.

## CBO does not see it by 2055 either

Everything turns on which ruler you pick up.
Measured gross, the gap to Social Security has already narrowed to under $200 billion and a crossover looks close.
Measured as the budget line, the Congressional Budget Office's long-term outlook puts net interest at 5.4% of gross domestic product in 2055 against 6.0% for Social Security. Three decades out, Social Security is still larger.
Mix the two figures and you get "soon to be first." Use one of them consistently and you get "still second in thirty years."
The books on this fiscal year close in mid-October.

## The theme is the year's worry

Jackson Hole is a three-day gathering that the Kansas City Fed, one of the twelve regional Federal Reserve banks, has hosted since 1978.
Only about a hundred people are invited, mostly central bank governors and academic economists, and press access is kept deliberately small.
The Kansas City Fed also picks the theme, which is why the theme tends to show what the Fed is worrying about that year.

In 2024 it was "Reassessing the Effectiveness and Transmission of Monetary Policy." In 2025 it was "Labor Markets in Transition: Demographics, Productivity, and Macroeconomic Policy."
How far to move rates, and how work itself is changing, were the questions of the past two years.

This year it is payments.

One step of explanation makes clear why that belongs on a central bankers' agenda.
A stablecoin is a token that moves on a blockchain while its value is pinned one to one to a currency such as the dollar.
That is the definition, and the part central banks care about comes right after it.
Once people start paying each other with the token instead of through a bank account, the question of who controls the payment rails changes hands.
The channel a central bank uses to steer the economy also runs through bank deposits and bank lending, so money that circulates outside that channel is money policy reaches less easily.

## Warsh called it a blank page

Kevin Warsh was sworn in as Fed chair on May 22, 2026. This is his first Jackson Hole in the job.
Asked at the July 29 FOMC press conference how he was preparing the speech, he said it looked to him "like a blank piece of paper right now," and that he had not begun consideration.

The current exclusion on gains from a primary home is $250,000 for a single filer and $500,000 for a couple, set in 1997 and never indexed since.
That exclusion is the example the indexing camp reaches for most often.

## Before the November midterms, statute or regulation

If it arrives as a bill, the question is a vote count in Congress.
If it arrives as a Treasury regulation, it meets the 1992 opinion and Loper Bright from the day it takes effect.

So the life expectancy of this tax cut is set by its form rather than its rate.
As a regulation, even one in force leaves after-tax returns impossible to pencil in until the litigation ends; as legislation, passage itself is the answer.
Which of the two shows up is the thing to watch before November.

## Why glass substrates matter

The board a chip sits on is called a substrate.
Today it is built by stacking layers of a plastic-based material.

The wider you make that board, the more it bows, and heat makes it stretch.
The chip does not stretch, so when only the board does, the thousands of joints connecting the two go out of line.

Glass stays flat and stretches far less under heat.
That lets a package carry bigger chips packed closer together.
Put simply, the industry has been stacking heavy things on a soft wooden cutting board, and glass swaps that board for marble.

The catch is that glass cracks.
The customer who will buy the chips runs its own tests: hundreds of heat and cool cycles to see whether the board fractures, and pressure tests to see whether it holds.
That process is called reliability evaluation.

## The reliability evaluation is where this stopped

According to industry officials quoted in the original post, the halt came because Samsung Electro-Mechanics did not obtain reliability certification from a global communications chip customer.

Deposition equipment has the longest gap between order and delivery.
